messages.subject: Speeding up GGPlot2 plotting...
parts:
In the example below it appears that qplot requires the following amount of time on an XP machine with 3.25 GB of RAM and 3.0 GHz Duo:
> ptm_qplot_time
   user  system elapsed
  17.62    1.11   19.34
 
For the example below is there a way to speed up the amount of time required for ggplot2? 
 
I'm curious about any possible shortcuts for accelerating the amount of time required to produce the plots using ggplot2.
 
Thank you for any feedback any insight that can be provided.
 
 
sample_size<-200
Home_SqFootage<-sample(1200:3600, size=sample_size, rep=T)
Home_Year_Built<-sample(1989:2008, size=sample_size, rep=T)
Home_Year_Sold<-sample(1989:2008, size=sample_size, rep=T)
Home_DF<-data.frame(SqFootage=Home_SqFootage, YearBuilt=as.character(Home_Year_Built), YearSold=as.character(Home_Year_Sold))
label_length<-length(unique(Home_DF$YearBuilt))
all_labels<-sort(unique(Home_DF$YearBuilt))
new_label<-NULL
for(ii in 1:label_length)
{
        if(ii%%2 == 0)
        {
                new_label_tmp<-as.character(all_labels[ii])
        } else {
                new_label_tmp<-c("")
        }      
       
        new_label<-c(new_label, new_label_tmp)
}
ptm_qplot<-proc.time()
qplot(YearBuilt, data = Home_DF, binwidth = 1, fill = factor(Home_DF$SqFootage)) +
                     scale_fill_discrete("Sq Footage") +
                     scale_y_continuous("Counts") +
                     scale_x_discrete("Year Built", labels=new_label)
ptm_qplot_time<-proc.time() - ptm_qplot

messages.subject: Re: Speeding up GGPlot2 plotting...
parts:
Here are some timing results for using qplot and ggplot2.  

ptm_qplot_9<-proc.time()
require(nlme, quiet = TRUE, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
model <- lme(height ~ age, data = Oxboys, random = ~ 1 + age | Subject)
oplot <- ggplot(data=Oxboys, aes(x=age, y=height, group=Subject)) + geom_line()
age_grid <- seq(-1, 1, length = 10)
subjects <- unique(Oxboys$Subject)
preds <- expand.grid(age = age_grid, Subject = subjects)
preds$height <- predict(model, preds)
oplot + geom_line(data = preds, colour = "#3366FF", size= 0.4)
ptm_qplot_9_time<-proc.time() - ptm_qplot_9
ptm_qplot_9_time
# Results
# user  system elapsed
#  1.543   0.033   1.640


ptm_qplot_12<-proc.time()
mpg2 <- subset(mpg, cyl != 5 & drv %in% c("4", "f"))
qplot(cty, data = mpg2, geom="histogram", binwidth = 2) + facet_grid(cyl ~ .)
ptm_qplot_12_time<-proc.time() - ptm_qplot_12
ptm_qplot_12_time
# Results
# user  system elapsed
#  1.861   0.027   1.935

I am very happy with these numbers but looking for a way to speed it up a little more.     Is there a way to allocate more priority to R when using the ggplot2 package or another approach?   These numbers are really good, so any suggestions to make them a tad better is very much helpful.

preds <- expand.grid(age = age_grid, Subject = subjects)

oplot + geom_line(data = preds, colour = "#3366FF", size= 0.4)
ptm_qplot_9_time<-proc.time() - ptm_qplot_9
